payload.text: The Brennecke Institute developed a thalliline-doped sodium-flow battery intended to reduce electrolyte crossover, a major aging mechanism in sodium-flow systems. An independent teardown audit corrected the prototype’s cycle life to 8,400 cycles to the 80% capacity knee, retracting the earlier 12,000-cycle claim because it used un-normalized depth-of-discharge data. The battery has a gravimetric energy density of 148 Wh/kg and a projected stack-level cost of $61/kWh at 500 MWh manufacturing scale. Its operating-temperature floor is 4 °C, below which the thalliline dopant precipitates from the negative electrolyte and cycling must stop.

FLAGS: Source A and the superseded pre-audit draft cite “12,000 cycles,” while finalized Source C corrects this to “8,400 cycles”; the summary reflects the governing corrected figure.
VERDICT: APPROVE
